ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Friedrich Nietzsche — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Four-week review after starting galcanezumab and the taper: withdrawal, headache days, acute medicine and the second injection

text.paragraph: Four-week review after starting galcanezumab and the butalbital taper. [S]

Mr. Nietzsche returns four weeks after the consultation. He finished the taper eight days ago. In the first ten days of the taper his headaches were worse, with six days in a row of headache and vomiting on two, as he had been warned; since then they have eased. His diary shows 14 headache days in the past four weeks, 8 with migraine features, and only 2 headache days in the eight days since the last tablet. Apart from the scheduled taper doses he used acute medicine on 6 days: naproxen on 6, with metoclopramide on 3. He had no tremor, sweating, confusion or seizure; his sleep was worse for a few nights in the second week. The nurse phone check planned for the end of the first taper week did not take place. The first galcanezumab injection left a small red patch for a day. His constipation is no worse. The floaters in his right eye from two weeks ago are fading, with no new flashes. He has had contact lenses fitted and reads more comfortably with the left eye. He has had two CBT-I sessions and sleeps about five hours. [S]

S — Synthetic diagnosis made at the consultation, anchored to his documented use of many medicines and sedatives; not a claim about his real medicines.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Headache Classification Committee of the International Headache Society (IHS). The International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (2018); The American Headache Society Consensus Statement: Update on integrating new migraine treatments into clinical practice (2021); Calcitonin gene-related peptide-targeting therapies are a first-line option for the prevention of migraine: An American Headache Society position statement update (2024); European Academy of Neurology guideline on the management of medication-overuse headache (2020); European Headache Federation guideline on the use of monoclonal antibodies targeting the calcitonin gene related peptide pathway for migraine prevention - 2022 update (2022); Choosing wisely in headache medicine: the American Headache Society's list of five things physicians and patients should question (2013); Refractive Errors Preferred Practice Pattern (2023); Posterior Vitreous Detachment, Retinal Breaks, and Lattice Degeneration Preferred Practice Pattern (2025); Behavioral and psychological treatments for chronic insomnia disorder in adults: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline (2021); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monograph (2026)

Follow-up: Preventive visit in two weeks. Eight-week review in four weeks with the third galcanezumab injection and the repeat dilated eye examination. Same-day eye care for new flashes, a shower of floaters or a shadow. Next scheduled visit 1881-09-01: periodic adult preventive visit. [S]
